text: Ava (Design): mock attached — trying to land a compact form pattern for nested settings. question: do we use a persistent required marker + optional tooltip, or hide the marker and show inline microcopy next to the field? trying to keep density tight while keeping it clear for keyboard/screen readers. Pt: destructive confirm also needs a short pattern suggestion. Liam (Product): i like the compact look but worried if hiding the marker will spike support asks. can we measure how often users miss required fields today? Diego (Eng): technically both are easy. for screen readers we'd prefer an explicit marker and `aria-required="true"` on the input. if we hide visual marker we still should expose the requirement via accessible name/aria. Priya (Accessibility): +1 to Diego. if you hide visual marker, ensure the label includes required state programmatically. e.g. `` and `input aria-required="true"`. Also announce inline errors with `role="alert"` so NVDA/VoiceOver picks them up immediately. Sam (PM): for destructive confirms (delete pool, wipe cache) what's the lightweight pattern? a modal with inline checkbox "i understand" or force typing the resource name? Ava (Design): proposal: use persistent, micro-asterisk that is subtle (low contrast) + tooltip on hover/tap explaining what required means. inline microcopy only for dense rows where label space is constrained (e.g., bulk rows). destructive: default to 2-step modal: first modal with clear consequences + checkbox "I understand"; only for especially dangerous ops require typing the resource ID. Diego (Eng): implementation nit: checkbox state can be focus-trapped inside modal and gate the primary button. avoid relying on `disabled` attribute alone for accessibility — set `aria-disabled` and still prevent submit on server. also add `data-confirmation-mode="checkbox"` or "type-to-confirm" for telemetry. Priya (Accessibility): for the modal pattern make sure the confirmation checkbox is reachable by keyboard and announced. If you require typing, validate with `aria-invalid` and expose helpful error text. Also ensure the modal restores focus to the triggering element on close. Liam (Product): sounding good. are we comfortable with the subtle asterisk for legal/regulation customers? they sometimes expect explicit 'required' word. Ava (Design): option: show explicit "required" label for enterprise/strict-compliance themes via a config flag, keep asterisk for standard. toggleable via design token `--form-required-verbosity`. Diego (Eng): fine with that. adds a tiny runtime flag in config. I'll stub the prop: `requiredVerbosity: 'asterisk' | 'word'` and wire to `
